alignments.note: Waw → but (rule 14).
Finite verb with its dummy subject and auxiliary, discontinuous around the negative (rule 25); head on the lexical verb.
לֹא → not; the ASV writes the negation and the verb as separate words, so rule 2 splits.
Predicate adjective → well.
Preposition → with.
Assimilated article morpheme → the (rule 12).
Substantival adjective → wicked.
Waw plus לֹא rendered by the single word neither, headed on the negative (rule 35).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rule 17).
No suffix or other possessive morpheme stands on יָמִים, so the supplied his is added (rule 18's closing sentence). The edition's italics corroborate without deciding.
Noun → days.

The comparative phrase is recast as a relative clause; the supplied relative and copula belong to the attributive relation the preposition carries, and the unit heads on the word realizing the preposition (rules 41, 49). The competing reading marks the italic which are added under rule 55.
The ASV renders the noun indefinitely and writes no the for this article (rule 29).
The indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15).
אֲשֶׁר → because (rule 14's open list read off the ASV).
Existential negative supplies the not, headed on the negation (rule 50).
Suffix takes the referential subject pronoun (rules 18, 50).
Participle rendered by a finite verb.
מִלִּפְנֵי rendered by the single word before; fused and headed on the construct noun carrying the lexeme (rules 30, 23).
Noun → God.

review_notes: The italic his before days answers to no morpheme and is added; the italic which are is read as part of the comparative phrase's recasting under rule 41's articleless-attributive sentence, with rule 49 supplying the copula on the preposition.
Both fused negatives follow rule 35, headed on the negative in each case.
